first_impression.reaction: The title smelled like clickbait ('You Did Not Know?'), but then the second sentence admits that 'several customs repeated online have no Portuguese source at all'. That's what kept me on the page. Most of these lists just copy each other, so a page saying which bits are made up is worth reading. I jumped to the FAQ and the legal section first, then went back.

journey.quote: What Are the Portuguese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
journey.reaction: Reads like a listicle headline. It nearly put me off, and it doesn't match how careful the rest of the page is.

journey.quote: Portuguese wedding traditions are quieter and more local than most lists suggest, and several customs repeated online have no Portuguese source at all.
journey.reaction: Good. That's the catch spelled out before I had to ask. It's the reason I kept reading.

journey.quote: Two to four witnesses may take part, but they are not compulsory.
journey.reaction: It's an actual rule, it's specific, and it goes against what the tradition implies. I can check that.

journey.section: Rice and petals as you leave
journey.quote: The meaning usually given, plenty and a fruitful marriage, is often told rather than recorded, and many venues now ask for petals only.
journey.reaction: The first half is honest. 'Many venues now ask for petals only' is a claim with nothing behind it, though. Which venues? Portuguese ones or Australian ones?

journey.section: Customs that are often told but hard to trace
journey.quote: Portuguese-language search results for the custom come almost entirely from Brazilian sites, and one Brazilian bridal magazine calls it Brazilian in origin.
journey.reaction: This is the best part of the page. They checked, they show how, and they don't overstate it. This is the kind of thing I'd post on Reddit.

journey.quote: Smartraveller notes that Portuguese government pages in English are often out of date or inaccurate, so confirm current requirements directly.
journey.reaction: Dated, sourced, and it admits its own limits. Exactly what I want before reading legal steps.

journey.section: Documents and the Australian Embassy in Lisbon
journey.quote: The embassy says the marriage must take place within three months of approval; IRN and the Justice portal say six months.
journey.reaction: Flagging where the official sources disagree, instead of quietly picking one, is the most credible thing a planner can do.

journey.quote: Australians marrying legally in Portugal start the process in person at a civil registry office with a certificate of no impediment, and should allow at least a month.
journey.reaction: Further down, the page says the embassy CNI 'processing takes a minimum of four weeks', and that you need it before you start the month-long registry process. So these steps follow one another, and 'at least a month' looks too short. If I'd built my timeline on that line I'd be annoyed.

journey.quote: Smartraveller's overall level for Portugal is "Exercise normal safety precautions" as at November 2026, and the legal path for Australians is clear if you start early.
journey.reaction: 'Clear' is generous when the same page has just shown me two points where the sources disagree. I'd say 'manageable'.

journey.quote: You have one Advisor as a single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing up front is a decent start, and the CTA comes after the evidence, not before. It still doesn't tell me how the fee works or whether you take a cut from suppliers. I'd find that out on another page before I enquired.

journey.quote: Whether you are marrying in the Douro or bringing your grandmother's filigree to a wedding at home, the details are what make it yours.
journey.reaction: Filler. Harmless, but it's the one line that sounds like marketing.

unanswered_questions: Realistic end-to-end lead time for the legal paperwork: CNI (minimum four weeks) plus the registry's one month. Is that roughly two to three months in practice?
How is the Wedded Advisor fee calculated (flat, percentage, tiered)?
Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues or suppliers in Portugal?
Has Wedded Wonderland actually run weddings in Portugal? Is there a real example with the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Portuguese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Clickbait-style title, and it doesn't match the careful, sourced tone of the body.

turn_offs_found.quote: many venues now ask for petals only
turn_offs_found.why: An unsupported claim on a page that otherwise sources everything. It stands out.

would_share_with: r/weddingplanning thread on destination weddings in Portugal

cta_reaction.quote: If the paperwork feels like the part that could unravel the plan, speak with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after real evidence and says the fee is agreed in writing, which I respect. But I won't enquire until I know the fee model and whether you take supplier commissions. I'd go and look for that on another page rather than ask in an enquiry.

top_3_changes: Fix the timeline: the takeaway and FAQ say 'allow at least a month', but CNI processing (minimum four weeks) comes before the registry's one-month lead time. State the realistic combined lead time.
Retitle so it doesn't read as clickbait. Something closer to the honest angle, e.g. what's documented versus what's only told.
Cut or source 'many venues now ask for petals only', and soften 'the legal path for Australians is clear' given the source conflicts the page itself flags.
